projects.title: Shadow Replay: A Postgres Workload Capture and Replay Proxy
projects.pitch: Build a small TCP proxy that sits in front of Postgres, records every query with its session, timestamp, and latency, and then replays the capture against a second database. Replay can run at 1x, 5x, or 'as fast as possible' while keeping each session's ordering intact. You then diff latency percentiles and result checksums between the two runs. It is a scaled-down version of what Airbnb uses to de-risk upgrades and migrations.
stack: Parquet or SQLite for capture storage
you_will_learn: Parsing a real database wire protocol and proxying it transparently
Preserving per-session ordering while replaying sessions concurrently (causality vs throughput)
Why time-scaled replay surfaces lock contention and connection-pool limits that synthetic benchmarks miss
Handling non-determinism (now(), sequences, random) and filtering writes so replay is safe
Comparing latency distributions (p50/p99) instead of averages for capacity planning
milestones: Pass-through proxy that logs startup and simple-query messages with timestamps and session IDs
Capture the extended query protocol (Parse/Bind/Execute) and persist captures to Parquet
Replayer that keeps per-session order, adds a time-scale factor, and caps concurrency
Result checksumming plus a latency diff report comparing Postgres 15 and 17
Add an incident-reproduction mode: replay just a time window and flag queries whose plans or latency regressed

projects.title: Mini-NTS: Authenticated Time with Stateless Cookies
projects.pitch: Implement a minimal Network Time Security (RFC 8915) server and client. It covers the NTS-KE handshake over TLS, the NTP packets carrying authenticated extension fields, and the stateless cookie scheme Meta describes, where sealing keys come from HKDF(master secret, epoch day) instead of being replicated. Run several server replicas that share no state and confirm any of them can validate any cookie. Then attack the system with delay injection to see what NTS does not protect against.
you_will_learn: Designing stateless servers by deriving keys rather than synchronizing them
Key rotation windows and accepting both the current and previous epoch keys
Integrity of NTP timestamps vs the unsolved delay/asymmetry attack
Why authenticated time matters as certificate lifetimes shrink (the bootstrapping chicken-and-egg)
Interop testing against a production implementation
milestones: Plain SNTP server and client that compute offset and round-trip delay
NTS-KE over TLS 1.3: negotiate the AEAD and hand out cookies
Authenticated NTP extension fields; reject tampered packets
HKDF epoch-day key derivation across 3 stateless replicas behind a UDP load balancer
Delay-attack harness (tc netem) showing how far an attacker can skew a client, and how multi-server sampling limits the skew

projects.title: Trigram Disk Indexer: Millisecond File and Content Search
projects.pitch: Build a whole-directory search tool in the spirit of fsearch. It does fuzzy filename matching with typo tolerance plus indexed content grep. Filenames go into an in-memory structure, content goes into an on-disk trigram inverted index, and the index stays fresh through filesystem events instead of rescans. Benchmark it on a million or more files and work toward sub-10ms queries.
you_will_learn: Inverted indexes and trigram posting lists (the idea behind Google Code Search and zoekt)
Compressed posting lists with roaring bitmaps and fast intersection
Memory-mapped, immutable index segments plus a mutable delta, merged LSM-style
Incremental indexing consistency: handling renames, event coalescing, and dropped events
Fuzzy matching (edit distance and subsequence scoring) and ranking under a latency budget
milestones: Parallel directory walker that builds a filename index; fuzzy subsequence search with scoring
Trigram content index for text files, with candidate verification by regex
Serialize the index as mmap-able immutable segments; measure cold vs warm query latency
Live updates via filesystem events into a delta segment, with background compaction
Benchmark suite (p50/p99 query latency, index size, rebuild time) and a write-up of the trade-offs

projects.title: Incremental Spreadsheet Recalc Engine in Rust
projects.pitch: Write the core of a spreadsheet engine, the part GridCraft has to get right. It needs a formula parser, a cell dependency graph, and incremental recalculation that only recomputes dirty cells, in topological order, with cycle detection. Then make it fast on a 1M-cell sheet and add parallel evaluation of independent subgraphs.
stack: egui or a WASM web front end (optional)
you_will_learn: Dependency graphs, topological sort, and dirty-propagation (the core of build systems and reactive dataflow)
Cycle detection and error propagation semantics (#REF!, #CIRC!)
Range references and why naive per-cell edges blow up memory (interval and range indexing)
Parallelizing a DAG safely by computing levels or using a work-stealing scheduler
Undo/redo as an operation log, the basis for collaboration later
milestones: Formula lexer and parser (arithmetic, cell refs, ranges, SUM/IF) to an AST
Dependency graph with full recalculation and cycle detection
Incremental recalc: mark dirty, recompute only affected cells in topo order; benchmark against full recalc
Efficient range dependencies for things like SUM(A1:A100000) without 100k edges
Parallel recalc with rayon plus an operation log for undo/redo; optional minimal grid UI

projects.title: Safe AI Reply Dispatcher: State Machines, Idempotency, and Circuit Breakers
projects.pitch: Build a support-reply service where an LLM only drafts replies. A human approves a specific revision, and an explicit state machine dispatches it through a flaky email provider. Timeouts move a message to delivery_unknown, and a reconciliation job resolves it instead of blindly retrying. Wrap the LLM and the provider in circuit breakers and output quality gates. Then run fault-injection experiments to prove you never double-send or send unapproved text.
stack: Any LLM API or a local model via Ollama
you_will_learn: Modeling workflows as explicit state machines with guarded transitions
Idempotency keys vs request fingerprints (from Sam Newman's discussion) and the transactional outbox pattern
Handling ambiguous outcomes: delivery_unknown, reconciliation, and why retries cause duplicates
Authorization bound to a revision hash so an edited draft needs re-approval; prompt-injection boundaries
Circuit breakers, fail-open vs fail-closed choices, and structured audit logging
milestones: Data model and state machine: drafted, approved(rev), dispatching, sent / delivery_unknown / failed
LLM drafting behind a quality gate (schema, PII and policy checks); injected instructions in a ticket cannot trigger a send
Outbox worker with idempotency keys against a mock provider that sometimes times out after succeeding
Reconciliation job, circuit breakers on the LLM and the provider, and OpenTelemetry traces across the flow
Fault-injection test suite (latency, drops, 500s, LLM garbage) asserting zero double-sends and zero unapproved sends
